idiom.title: At the end of your rope
idiom.interpretationEn: This phrase originates from farm work, referring to the point where a rope has reached its maximum length. It symbolizes someone having exhausted all means or patience. It is often used to convey extreme fatigue or helplessness.
idiom.interpretationZh: 这个短语源自农场工作，用来表示一条绳子到了尽头。比喻某人已经使尽了最后的手段或忍耐到了极限。通常用于表达极度的疲劳或无助。

examples.en: I’m really at the end of my rope with this project; nothing seems to work.
examples.zh: 我对这个项目真的走投无路了；没有什么方案有效。

examples.en: She was at the end of her rope, unable to find a solution to her problems.
examples.zh: 她已经忍无可忍，无法找到解决问题的方法。

examples.en: John is at the end of his rope with his job; he can’t take it anymore.
examples.zh: 约翰对他的工作已经忍无可忍了；他再也受不了了。

people.name: Louis III, Prince of Condé
people.extract: Louis III de Bourbon, Prince of Condé was a prince du sang as a member of the reigning House of Bourbon at the French court of Louis XIV. Styled as Duke of Bourbon from birth, he succeeded his father in 1709 as Prince of Condé ; however, he was still known by the ducal title. He was prince for less than a year.
highlights: Prince du sang at French court of Louis XIV.
Succeeded father as Prince of Condé in 1709.
Styled as Duke of Bourbon from birth.

people.name: Hans-Rudolf Merz
people.extract: Hans-Rudolf Merz is a Swiss politician who served as President of Switzerland in 2009. He concurrently served as a member of the Federal Council from 2004 to 2010 for the Free Democratic Party.
highlights: Served as President of Switzerland in 2009.

people.name: John Bevis
people.extract: John Bevis was an English medical doctor, electrical researcher and astronomer. He is best known for discovering the Crab Nebula in 1731. He was educated at Christ Church, Oxford, being awarded his B.A. in 1715 and his M.A. in 1718.
highlights: English medical doctor, electrical researcher, and astronomer.
